disease_label_per_paper: Acute HEV infection with Guillain-Barre syndrome and respiratory failure

past_medical_history: type 2 diabetes mellitus without known microvascular complications

presentation_summary: 72-year-old man presented with symmetric numbness and weakness in both lower limbs with difficulty walking that began on awakening and rapidly progressed to involve both upper limbs symmetrically.

He had been discharged the day before after elective cataract surgery. Initial neurologic exam showed relatively symmetric lower-limb paraparesis with grade 4/5 strength, diminished sensation in a stocking-glove distribution, no cranial nerve changes, no meningeal signs, and otherwise unremarkable physical exam.

Laboratory tests showed acute hepatocellular injury with AST 1834 U/L, ALT 2139 U/L, LDH 954 U/L, ALP 119 U/L, GGT 527 U/L, total bilirubin 1.2 mg/dL, anti-HEV IgM 3.63 UI/mL, anti-HEV IgG 0.66 UI/mL, and HEV viral load 1,977,133 UI/mL; hepatitis A, B, C, D, other viral serologies, and autoimmune studies were negative.
Abdominal ultrasound showed slightly increased echogenicity suggestive of steatohepatitis.

He deteriorated with worsening quadriparesis, hyporeflexia, dysphagia, and dyspnea. Lumbar puncture showed albuminocytologic dissociation with CSF protein 76 mg/dL and leukocytes less than 3/mm3; electromyography showed decreased conduction velocities suggestive of generalized demyelinating polyneuropathy.

He was diagnosed with Guillain-Barre syndrome and started on IVIg 0.4 g/kg/day, but continued to deteriorate and developed respiratory failure requiring endotracheal intubation and mechanical ventilation.

After a five-day IVIg course he gradually improved, was extubated on day 14, transferred to neurology ward, and discharged to rehabilitation. Liver enzymes normalized with supportive care and liver function remained preserved.

quality_warnings: The source reports HEV viral load in UI/mL; the project axis uses IU/mL and preserves the original unit spelling in source_text_value.
Discharge day is approximated as day 14 because extubation occurred on day 14 and the table labels discharge values without a separate exact day.
Neurologic treatment response and final recovery are preserved as course/confirmatory evidence rather than as HEV diagnostic shortcuts.
